phases.label: Period I: Early Harappan (Regional Hakra Culture Tradition)
phases.architecture: Pit dwellings, followed by floor levels and rectangular structures; attribution of the earliest excavated material is disputed within the report.

phases.label: Transition Period
phases.architecture: Small rectangular structures and hearths precede the mature plan.

phases.label: Period IIA
phases.architecture: Planned brick structural complexes, streets and storage areas.

phases.label: Period IIB
phases.architecture: Continued settlement with changed material and burial evidence.

phases.label: Period IIC
phases.architecture: Hypothesized final phase; its deposits are described as removed.

support.text: The excavator places well-planned structural complexes and streets at the beginning of Period IIA.

3.basis: Excavator explicitly bases the phase division on cultural comparison and says phase dates lack radiocarbon support.
3.rule: assignment: levels of evidence and candidate values
3.sigma_status: fixed assignment rule; not a newly fitted archaeological error

parts.notes: The later book also publishes calibrated determinations, but the cross-dated construction estimate is not presented as a radiocarbon-based start. Structural Phase numbers in the dating table have not been equated to cultural subperiod labels.

first_occupation.evidence: The cultural-sequence chapter proposes an early founding estimate from regional comparison; the final synthesis questions the early attribution of the excavated basal levels. Neither supplies an agreed site-specific calibrated founding boundary.

searches: Existing preliminary and final excavation reports, chronology chapter and AMS appendix; Bayesian boundary and newer dating searches.

disagreements.text: The preliminary and final excavation chronologies differ in the start of the planned town. The final summary also questions the basal Early Harappan attribution.
